exposure: improved population distribution of glucose tolerance
Simulated one standard deviation decrease in glucose values
cohort: 3217 women with mild glucose intolerance, delivered at The University of North Carolina Women's Hospital from April 1996 to May 2010
finding: Modestly improving the population distribution of glucose tolerance in pregnancies affected by mild glucose intolerance could translate to meaningful improvements in perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were predicted to decrease from 30.1% to 26.4% with improved glucose tolerance.
